short: Ten thousand Swedes broke a Russian army several times their size in a blizzard.
full:
Peter I had been besieging the Swedish fortress of Narva in Ingria since October with an army usually put at around 37,000 men. Charles XII landed in Livonia and marched to relieve it with roughly 10,000, arriving on 30 November 1700 with his troops tired and short of food after a week on bad roads.

A snowstorm blew straight into the Russian lines in the early afternoon. The Swedes attacked in two columns under cover of it, broke through the extended siege works in under half an hour, and rolled the Russian army up against the Narva river, where a pontoon bridge collapsed under the weight of the retreat. Russian dead ran to perhaps 9,000 against a few hundred Swedish. Peter, who had left the camp the day before, treated the result as an argument for rebuilding his army from the foundations, and did so. The date given is Gregorian: Sweden's own calendar, one day ahead of the Julian, made it 20 November, and Russian accounts say the 19th.
